bullets.title: Bessent eyes $1T Treasury General Account for bond buybacks to tame long-end yields
bullets.body: Senior Treasury officials told CNBC that Secretary Bessent could tap nearly $1 trillion from the Treasury General Account to fund expanded bond buybacks, including potentially doubling purchases of longer-dated bonds. The move is aimed at containing long-end yields rather than restarting QE. MS CIO Wilson characterized the buybacks as 'maintaining market functioning,' while markets await Friday's Jackson Hole speech from Fed Chair Warsh for additional rate direction.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole / Warsh speech Friday: markets testing the Fed's tolerance on long rates
bullets.body: Analysts flagged Chair Warsh's Friday Jackson Hole address as the week's key macro event. Bond markets have been pushing longer-term yields higher (10-year at 4.71-4.72%) in what some describe as 'testing' the Fed. 22V Research argued a hawkish Warsh signal would actually reduce 10-year vol and support longer-duration assets, while JPM viewed Jackson Hole as a likely non-event.

bullets.title: Oil spike is the single biggest tail risk to US equities per Morgan Stanley Wilson
bullets.body: MS CIO Michael Wilson identified an oil price spike as the largest near-term risk to US stocks, warning it could fuel inflation and force Fed tightening. Brent rose 6.6% to $94.39 over the prior two weeks on Hormuz closure/Iran sanctions fears, with distillate inventories at a 30-year seasonal low; front-month diesel crack hit an all-time intraday high above $102 vs. a $20-30 historical norm. Wilson recommends energy equities as the best portfolio hedge against the risk.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions: crude quiet today but structural energy disruption persists
bullets.body: Total's CEO said crude is moving through Hormuz 'very quietly' today, but Hormuz weekly transits collapsed to 73 from 91 the prior week with no VLCCs or LNG crossing Aug 20. IEA chief Birol ruled out a second SPR release (the March release was 400M barrels, 20% of reserves), while Shell's CEO warned the market's 'shock absorber' capacity is weakening. Iran's rial hit a record low of 2M rials/dollar amid escalating US sanctions.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings Wed: buy-side bars $94-95B revenue, $107-108B+ guide; price hikes 15%+ early 2027
bullets.body: Consensus across UBS, JPM, Rosenblatt, and Cantor: NVDA is expected to beat FQ2 (Jul) revenue by ~$3-4B to ~$94-95B and guide FQ3 to $107-108B on Blackwell stability and Rubin ramping. NVDA is notifying customers of >15% price hikes on Grace Blackwell/Vera Rubin systems in early 2027 due to soaring memory costs, with the intent to sustain 70%+ gross margins. Cantor maintained Overweight/$350 PT citing underweight investor positioning that could drive a very sharp rally.

bullets.title: NVDA's $6B Poolside deal and Perplexity stake: building a US open-weight model to compete with China
bullets.body: NVDA offered a $6B license of Poolside's Model Factory plus hires of 109 engineers and a $1B equity investment at $12B pre-money to accelerate Nemotron as an open-source alternative to DeepSeek/Kimi. NVDA is also in talks to invest multi-billions in Perplexity at a $30B+ valuation. The strategy positions NVDA as a model-layer competitor to OpenAI and Anthropic, and locks in critical AI talent ahead of rivals.

bullets.title: DRAM/NAND in supercycle: spot prices +5-11% monthly, server DRAM contracts up 58-63% q/q
bullets.body: DRAM spot prices surged 5-11% monthly; Q2 contract DRAM rose 58-63% q/q after a 90-95% surge in Q1. NVDA is passing through >15% cost increases to customers. TrendForce expects server DRAM contracts to rise another 13-18% in Q3, while one supplier warns DRAM supply to module makers could fall to 30% of 2026 levels next year. SNDK and WDC fell 9.8% and 7.4% respectively in Canadian pre-market trading.

bullets.title: AI capex narrative under pressure: unit economics deteriorating, circular financing concerns rising
bullets.body: JPM and Jefferies flagged that AI capital demand remains strong but unit economics are deteriorating—Anthropic's Fable 5 demand is flagging as customers opt for cheaper models, OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Sol prices >20%, and DeepSeek eliminated peak pricing. Multiple capital raises (BABA $10B, AAOI $600M ATM, SoftBank $6.3B bond, XPEV $900M) signal intensifying capital competition. Wolfe Research warned rising long-term yields could pressure hyperscaler AI spending, which is debt-financed.

bullets.title: Data center political backlash surges ahead of midterms; ~75% of Americans oppose local DC development
bullets.body: ~75% of Americans now oppose local data center development, with Texas Governor Abbott reversing his stance and Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro issuing an executive order. Jefferies noted AI regulation, data center pushback (TX, NY), and state-level policy will be key political issues heading into the November midterms. ERCOT's August 31 provisional designation decision is positive for HUT, CIFR, GLXY, and MARA, with a final PUCT decision expected December 17.

bullets.title: Gold breaks out to new highs; Fidelity PM doubles allocation on Fed policy uncertainty
bullets.body: Gold broke out to bullish TRADE and TREND signals per Hedgeye (risk range $4,403-$4,694), rallying alongside Bitcoin as the macro regime shifted from Quad 4 to Quad 3. A Fidelity PM doubled gold holdings over three weeks citing Fed policy uncertainty. ETFs are adding holdings and China's central bank is buying at the highest pace since 2023. The dollar's weakness is fueling the inverse correlation.

bullets.title: Sector rotation underway: quality/healthcare over semis/utilities; mega-cap tech de-grossing
bullets.body: Hedgeye shifted its portfolio from 6-7 semiconductor names to 2 semis + 6-8 software names. Healthcare (XLV) outperformed Utilities (XLU) by 1,100bps in August. MS Wilson flagged a quality rotation playing out, with high FCF/high gross margin baskets up 16% and 9% respectively over two months. Jefferies noted the largest mega-cap tech de-grossing in 2+ years, with positioning rotating toward quality and asset-light models.

bullets.title: Nominal GDP ~6% drives 10-year toward 5%; AI still net job creator per Lazar
bullets.body: Piper's Nancy Lazar argues that 6% nominal GDP growth explains the 10-year yield trajectory toward 5%, consistent with a six-decade pattern. She sees AI as a net job creator (legal, engineering, software hiring accelerating) and notes Taiwan's export orders to the US surged 88.6% YoY in July, with Taiwan manufacturing PMI having a 70% correlation to US ISM—flagging continued US manufacturing strength.

bullets.title: US-Canada trade war: 50% tariffs on $20B Canadian goods, retaliatory measures expected Sept 8
bullets.body: The US-Canada trade deal broke down, triggering 50% tariffs on $20B of Canadian goods, with Canada's PM Carney signaling retaliatory tariffs on September 8. OPCO noted this as positive for US steel producers (STLD +4.3%, NUE +3.5%) but negative for agricultural equipment. JPM described Canada/Iran trade war as 'heating up' and a macro headwind going into the week.

bullets.title: US H-1B visa $100K fee proposal: 1-6% FY27 EPS risk for Indian IT; ACN and large caps better positioned
bullets.body: The White House proposed a ~$100K fee on H-1B visa petitions for workers already in the US, applicable only to new petitions. Analysts estimate up to 6% FY27 earnings impact for Indian IT under worst-case assumptions, with large caps (TCS, Infosys, Accenture) better positioned given lower visa dependence. A 19-state coalition has filed suit under the APA.

bullets.title: CoreWeave GPU-cloud durability conviction drops sharply despite surging usage
bullets.body: A QSG survey found CoreWeave usage rose more than any other GPU-cloud provider, but 12-month spend increase intent collapsed from 90% to 43%, and 95% of users now see vulnerability to GPU supply fluctuations (up from 65%). Two-year outlook remains constructive at 85% expecting increased investment. Contracted compute prices surged from $10-12M/MW-yr to $25-50M/MW-yr, benefiting neocloud operators.

bullets.title: MRVL: Wells Fargo raises PT to $310; Google deal could imply $120B revenue over 5.5 years
bullets.body: Wells Fargo raised MRVL's price target to $310 from $240. Wolfe Research modeled the Google structured deal at ~$120B revenue potential over 5.5 years (~$20B/yr), describing it as transformative. JPM's buyside survey showed light positioning (1/5 score) with buy-side modeling ~15% sequential revenue growth; implied earnings move is 8.8%.

bullets.title: AI security spending accelerating: PANW launches Frontier AI Defense, Fortinet acquires Virtue AI
bullets.body: Palo Alto Networks launched the Frontier AI Critical Defense Program with OpenAI and Anthropic to identify AI-discovered vulnerabilities and deploy virtual patches. Fortinet acquired Virtue AI for agentic red-teaming and AI controls. NTT DATA and PANW signed a multi-year alliance targeting $1B in joint business by 2029. The security sector is up 24.7% YTD, outperforming S&P 500's 12.1%.

bullets.title: Consumer spending accelerating: +5.6% YoY MTD in August, discretionary +6%; upper income leading
bullets.body: JPM card data shows total consumer spending up 5.6% YoY in August MTD vs. +4.4% in July, with discretionary outpacing non-discretionary at +6.0%. Gen Z/Millennials lead at +8.7% YoY. However, gasoline/energy spend surged 18.3% YoY on prices +28.6%, disproportionately pressuring lower/middle income households.

bullets.title: PDD Q2: revenue 2% miss, EPS 4% beat; transaction services deceleration signals structural headwinds
bullets.body: PDD reported Q2 revenue of CNY112.4B vs. consensus CNY115.2B (miss), while adj. EPS of CNY19.33 beat consensus CNY18.45 on better investment income. Transaction services revenue grew 13% YoY but decelerated from 20% last quarter. EU low-value import duty changes are expected to hurt cross-border orders near-term. JPM maintains Neutral/$110 PT, forecasting only 8% adj. EPS growth in 2026.

bullets.title: AI productivity ROI still elusive at the index level; negative AI/non-AI stock correlation at 2020 extreme
bullets.body: Jefferies noted only 11% of S&P 500 companies quantified AI productivity gains in Q2, with just 2% showing direct earnings benefit. AI and non-AI stocks are now negatively correlated at the most extreme level since 2020, creating a binary either/or trade. Hedgeye's broader view: AI adoption is still early, with coding showing productivity gains but major consumer behavioral shifts not yet materializing.
